index.meta.title: Sprocket Player — Your media, your way. On Apple TV and iPad.
index.meta.description: Sprocket Player is a network media browser and player for Apple TV and iPad. Plays the movies, shows, photos and documents you already own straight from your NAS. No server, no account, no transcoding, no cloud.
hero.lede: Sprocket Player plays the movies, shows, photos and documents you already own, straight from the shares on your home network. No server to install. No account to create. Nothing leaves your house.
hero.requirements: Requires tvOS 18.6 or iPadOS 17.6 or later.
formats.lede: Sprocket Player is built on the VLC engine, so the MKVs, remuxes, and odd containers that trip up other players just work. Videos, photos and documents all live in one browser.
formats.video.title: Video
formats.video.body: Full-bitrate playback with multiple audio tracks, embedded and sidecar subtitles, and chapters.
formats.photos.title: Photos
formats.photos.body: Browse network photo folders or your iCloud Photos library. Slideshows with a timer, and any photo can become your wallpaper.
formats.docs.title: Documents & comics
formats.docs.body: Read PDFs, comic archives and text files from the couch, with page-by-page navigation on the Siri Remote or touch.
formats.sources: Sources: SMB and NFS network shares, plus the on-device Photos library. Shares are discovered automatically with Bonjour.
companion.lede: You've already organised your library and scraped the artwork. Sprocket Player reads the same folders those servers use, so you get posters, fanart, episode titles and plot summaries without running anything extra.
companion.point1: Understands standard Movies / TV Shows / Season folder layouts.
companion.point2: Reads Kodi-style NFO metadata and local artwork out of the box.
companion.point3: Optional Collections group a whole franchise into one folder.
companion.point4: Watched state and resume points live on the device. Hide what you've seen with one toggle.
companion.point5: Play trailers straight from the library.
companion.jellyfin: Point at the library share and go.
companion.kodi: NFO files and artwork, fully supported.
companion.caption: Kodi-scraped metadata, rendered on the big screen.
intro.lede: Turn on Intro Detection and Sprocket Player listens to a season in the background, fingerprints the title sequence, and finds it in every episode. When you hit it, a Skip Intro button is waiting.
intro.point1: Works on your own files, with no online database and no server plugin.
intro.point2: Analysis runs entirely on your Apple TV or iPad, while you browse.
intro.point3: New episodes are picked up automatically the next time you visit the season.
intro.point4: Off by default. Enable it in Options when you're ready.
intro.caption: Detected on device. No lookup, no upload.
direct.lede: Media servers re-encode video on the fly when a client can't handle it, burning CPU and softening the picture. Sprocket Player decodes on the device itself, so every stream is the original bitstream at full quality, straight off your NAS.
direct.point1: No server-side transcoder, no hardware-acceleration licence, no waiting for a session to spin up.
direct.point2: Your NAS only has to serve files. A basic share on any box is enough.
direct.point3: Switch audio tracks and subtitles instantly, with no re-encode.
direct.point4: Thumbnails are generated by the device too, and cached for next time.
direct.caption: Multiple audio tracks and subtitles, a swipe away.
privacy.lede: Sprocket Player has no backend, no account, and no cloud. It talks to your shares and nothing else. Privacy isn't a setting we added later. It's how the app is built.
privacy.local.title: Local only
privacy.local.body: No server component and no account. Your media and browsing history never leave your network.
privacy.keychain.title: Keychain credentials
privacy.keychain.body: Share usernames and passwords are stored in the system Keychain on the device, and nowhere else.
privacy.pin.title: PIN-secured sources
privacy.pin.body: Lock a source behind a PIN. Its thumbnails and history are encrypted at rest with AES-256, keyed from that PIN.
privacy.disconnect.title: Auto-disconnect
privacy.disconnect.body: Choose to drop share connections when you leave the app or go idle, so a shared living-room TV stays a shared TV.
privacy.note: The only outbound connection is anonymous crash reporting, which can be turned off in Options.
privacy.caption: Everything stays on the device, encrypted.
more.lede: Small things that add up to an app you actually want to open every night.
more.devices.title: Apple TV and iPad
more.devices.body: One app, designed for the Siri Remote at ten feet and for touch on the couch. Same library either way.
more.wallpapers.title: Wallpapers
more.wallpapers.body: Bundled photo and animated backgrounds, or long-press any photo in your library and make it the wallpaper.
more.sort.title: Sort your way
more.sort.body: Name, date, size, recently viewed or random. Favourites float to the top, and each folder remembers how you sorted it.
more.collections.title: Collections
more.collections.body: Group every film in a franchise into one folder, even the later ones that stopped following the naming pattern.
more.slideshows.title: Slideshows
more.slideshows.body: Turn any folder of photos into a timed slideshow, with a progress ring so you always know where you are.
more.localised.title: Localised
more.localised.body: Available in English, French, German, Italian, Spanish and Japanese.

support.faq.q1: Which devices does Sprocket Player run on?
support.faq.a1: Apple TV running tvOS 18.6 or later, and iPad running iPadOS 17.6 or later. It is not available for iPhone.
support.faq.q2: Does Sprocket Player need Plex, Jellyfin or Kodi installed?
support.faq.a2: No. It reads media straight from an SMB or NFS share. If you already use one of those servers, point Sprocket Player at the same folders and it will pick up your artwork and metadata.
support.faq.q3: Why do I get an “SMB2 or higher required” error from a Windows PC?
support.faq.a3: Sprocket Player uses SMB2 and above. Windows 10 and later have SMB1 disabled, but some older shares still advertise only SMB1. Enable SMB2 in Windows Features and try again.

policy.meta.title: Privacy Policy — Sprocket Player
policy.meta.description: What data Sprocket Player handles, and what happens to it. Local-only by design.
policy.title: Sprocket Player Privacy Policy
policy.intro: Sprocket Player is a media browser and player for iPad and Apple TV. This document describes what data the app handles and what happens to it.
policy.data.title: What Sprocket Player does with your data
policy.data.local: Sprocket Player connects to file shares on your local network (SMB, NFS) and reads from your device's photo library to display and play your photos and videos. The app does not have its own backend server, does not require an account, and does not transmit your media or browsing activity to us or to any third party.
policy.data.creds: Usernames and passwords for SMB and NFS shares you configure are stored locally on your device in the iOS/tvOS Keychain. They never leave your device.
policy.data.prefs: Your settings, source lists, watched-state, and generated thumbnails are stored locally on your device. When a source is marked as secured with a PIN, the associated thumbnails and preference records are encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM via Apple's CryptoKit. The encryption keys are derived from the PIN and stored in the Keychain.
policy.crash.title: Crash and performance data
policy.crash.p1_after: to capture crash reports and basic performance metrics. This data is sent to Sentry's servers, used only to identify and fix bugs, and is not linked to your identity or used for tracking.
policy.crash.p2: The categories of data Sentry collects:
policy.crash.li1: stack traces, device model, OS version, app version, and the state of the app at the moment of a crash
policy.crash.p3: No personally identifying information, no media files, no source credentials, and no contents of your photo library are ever sent to Sentry or anywhere else.
policy.network.title: Network access
policy.network.body: Sprocket Player uses your device's local network access to discover SMB shares via Bonjour and to connect to file shares you configure. iOS will prompt you to grant local network permission the first time the app needs it. The app does not connect to any servers on the public internet other than Sentry (for crash reporting, as described above).
policy.children.title: Children's privacy
policy.children.body: Sprocket Player is not directed at children under 13 and does not knowingly collect any personal information from children.
